artboards.title: Option B — Out on the Field

annotations.text:
Three directions for the homepage, plus how each looks on a phone.

The page is now: a brief introduction, latest news, and a link through to upcoming events. No event listings on the homepage.

Anything in [square brackets] is a placeholder — news titles, dates and authors come live from Spanner, so I haven't invented any. Everything else is real club copy.

What's making it feel cluttered today:

• The page opens with an <h1> that just says "Home"
• Everything sits at one size on one white slab — no hierarchy to follow
• News posts render full-length, so one long one buries the rest
• The 2.5MB background photo is only visible as a 12px margin
• 6 nav links + a two-line wordmark + an 80px logo all crammed into 1024px

OPTION A — CLUB GREEN
The careful fix.

Same structure and pages, but with a real intro, a proper type ramp and generous space. News is the body of the page; a green band at the foot carries the events link.

Why: lowest risk. Nobody in the club has to relearn anything, and it's the quickest to build.

Tradeoff: safe. It solves the clutter but nothing about it will stop a stranger scrolling past.

OPTION B — OUT ON THE FIELD
Lead with the mud.

Full-bleed photo hero carrying the introduction, then news set editorially, then a dark band with the events link.

Why: the club's best asset is what it looks like on a wet Sunday, and right now the site hides that behind a white box.

Tradeoff: it lives or dies on the photography — someone has to keep feeding it good pictures. Heaviest page of the three, and the news sits a full screen down.

OPTION C — NOTICEBOARD
Straight to the point.

No hero. A tight intro block, then news as the main column with a sidebar carrying the events link and a word for newcomers. Everything above the fold.

Why: for the hundred-plus existing members, news and what's-on are the only things they come for.

Tradeoff: coldest of the three to a newcomer, and it leans hardest on there being fresh news to show.
Phone views — worth weighing these heavily. Most people will meet this site on a phone, and the current one squeezes a 5em logo and a two-line wordmark into 390px before you reach any content.
